title.en: From the Cold War to Today

clips.send: Houston: Mission Control. 1965 – today, Texas. NASA’s Manned Spacecraft Center (now the Johnson Space Center) took over Mission Control for crewed flights starting with Gemini 4 in 1965. 20 July 1969: “Houston, Tranquility Base here. The Eagle has landed.” Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin walked on the Moon while Michael Collins orbited above. Twelve astronauts walked on the Moon between 1969 and 1972 — all of them American.

clips.send: Washington: containment and NATO. 1947, 1949, 1958. 1947: the Truman Doctrine promised help to countries resisting communism — a policy called containment (遏制). 4 April 1949: twelve countries signed the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington, creating NATO (北约): “an attack on one is an attack on all.”. 1958: after Sputnik, Congress created NASA. After the Cuban crisis, a Washington–Moscow “hotline” (1963) let leaders talk directly.

clips.send: Huntsville, Alabama: “Rocket City”. Marshall Space Flight Center, 1960. Wernher von Braun’s rocket team at the Redstone Arsenal built the rocket that launched Explorer 1. NASA’s Marshall Space Flight Center opened here in 1960 and developed the Saturn V Moon rocket. The Saturn V stood 363 feet (111 m) tall — taller than the Statue of Liberty with its pedestal. Today Huntsville hosts Space Camp.

clips.send: Cuban Missile Crisis. 16–28 October 1962. After its 1959 revolution, Cuba under Fidel Castro allied with the Soviet Union. A US U-2 spy plane photographed Soviet nuclear missile sites about 90 miles (145 km) from Florida. For 13 days the world held its breath. Kennedy ordered a naval “quarantine”. Khrushchev agreed to remove the missiles; the US promised not to invade Cuba and secretly agreed to remove its missiles from Turkey.

clips.send: Silicon Valley, California. 1971 – today. Named after the silicon used to make computer chips. In 1971 Intel released the first commercial microprocessor — a computer’s “brain” on one chip. 1976: Steve Jobs and Steve Wozniak founded Apple; the Apple II (1977) was one of the first popular home computers. IBM’s PC followed in 1981. 1998: Google was founded. 2007: Apple’s iPhone put the internet in people’s pockets.

clips.send: ARPANET: the first four nodes. 29 October 1969, California and Utah. ARPA, a Defense Department agency set up in 1958 after Sputnik, paid for a network linking university computers. The first message went from UCLA to SRI: they tried to type “LOGIN”, but the system crashed after “LO”. By December four sites were linked. It used packet switching: messages are chopped into small packets that each find their own way. In 1983 ARPANET switched to TCP/IP — the common language of today’s internet.

clips.send: Cape Canaveral and Kennedy Space Center. 1958 – today, Florida. 31 January 1958: Explorer 1, the first US satellite, launched here and discovered radiation belts around Earth. 5 May 1961: Alan Shepard became the first American in space. 20 February 1962: John Glenn became the first American to orbit Earth (3 orbits). 16 July 1969: Apollo 11 lifted off on a Saturn V rocket. Why Florida? It is far south, and rockets fly out over the ocean.

clips.send: Trinity test, New Mexico. 16 July 1945. Scientists of the secret Manhattan Project (based at Los Alamos) tested the first atomic bomb in the New Mexico desert. In August 1945 the US dropped atomic bombs on Hiroshima and Nagasaki; Japan surrendered and World War II ended. In 1949 the Soviet Union tested its own bomb. The nuclear arms race (军备竞赛) had begun.

clips.send: 11 September 2001. New York, Arlington, Virginia, Shanksville, Pennsylvania. Terrorists of the al-Qaeda group hijacked four passenger planes. Two struck the World Trade Center in New York and one struck the Pentagon. Passengers on United Flight 93 fought back; the plane crashed in a field near Shanksville, Pennsylvania. Nearly 3,000 people died that day. Afterwards the US created the Department of Homeland Security, tightened airport security and went to war in Afghanistan. Memorials stand at all three sites.

clips.send: 古巴导弹危机。1962年10月16日—28日。1959年革命后，卡斯特罗领导的古巴与苏联结盟。美国U-2侦察机拍到了苏联在古巴修建的核导弹发射场，距佛罗里达只有约90英里（145千米）。在13天里，全世界都屏住了呼吸。肯尼迪下令进行海上“隔离”（封锁）。赫鲁晓夫同意撤走导弹；美国承诺不入侵古巴，并秘密同意撤走部署在土耳其的导弹。

clips.send: 2001年9月11日。纽约 · 弗吉尼亚州阿灵顿 · 宾夕法尼亚州尚克斯维尔。恐怖组织“基地”组织的成员劫持了四架客机。两架撞向纽约世界贸易中心，一架撞向五角大楼。联合航空93号航班的乘客奋起反抗，飞机坠毁在宾夕法尼亚州尚克斯维尔附近的田野里。当天近3000人遇难。此后，美国成立了国土安全部，加强了机场安检，并出兵阿富汗。三个地点都建有纪念馆。

clips.send: 阿帕网：最早的四个节点。1969年10月29日 · 加利福尼亚州与犹他州。阿帕，A R P A，是1958年苏联卫星上天后美国国防部成立的机构，它出资建立了连接大学计算机的网络。第一条消息从加州大学洛杉矶分校发往斯坦福研究所：他们想输入“LOGIN”，系统却在“LO”之后崩溃了。到12月，四个地点连通。它采用“分组交换”：消息被切成小数据包，各自找路到达。1983年，阿帕网改用TCP/IP协议——这是今天互联网的通用“语言”。

clips.send: 卡纳维拉尔角与肯尼迪航天中心。1958年至今 · 佛罗里达州。1958年1月31日，美国第一颗卫星“探险者1号”从这里发射，发现了环绕地球的辐射带。1961年5月5日，艾伦·谢泼德成为第一个进入太空的美国人；1962年2月20日，约翰·格伦成为第一个绕地球轨道飞行的美国人（绕了3圈）。1969年7月16日，“阿波罗11号”乘“土星5号”火箭升空。为什么在佛罗里达？这里纬度低，火箭还可以飞向大海。

clips.send: 华盛顿：遏制政策与北约。1947年 · 1949年 · 1958年。1947年，“杜鲁门主义”宣布援助抵抗共产主义的国家——这被称为“遏制”（containment）政策。1949年4月4日，12个国家在华盛顿签署《北大西洋公约》，成立北约，N A T O：“对一国的攻击就是对全体的攻击。”。1958年，苏联卫星上天后，国会设立了美国国家航空航天局，N A S A。古巴危机后，1963年华盛顿和莫斯科之间开通了“热线”。
clips.text: 华盛顿：遏制政策与北约。1947年 · 1949年 · 1958年。1947年，“杜鲁门主义”宣布援助抵抗共产主义的国家——这被称为“遏制”（containment）政策。。1949年4月4日，12个国家在华盛顿签署《北大西洋公约》，成立北约（NATO）：“对一国的攻击就是对全体的攻击。”。1958年，苏联卫星上天后，国会设立了美国国家航空航天局（NASA）。古巴危机后，1963年华盛顿和莫斯科之间开通了“热线”。
